Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 1:

(p-399) Surat "al-Qamar" (The Moon)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split.﴾ "The Hour has drawn near": the Resurrection has come close.

"And the moon has been split": into two halves. It is also read "wa-qad inshaqqa" (and it has already been split), meaning: the Hour has drawn near, and among the signs of its nearness has occurred that the moon has been split, just as you say: "The prince has arrived, and the bearer of good news has already come with his arrival." Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I saw Hira between the two halves of the moon." It is also said that its meaning is: it will split on the Day of Resurrection. The majority hold the first view, and it is what is transmitted in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). One might say: if it had split, it would not have been hidden from the people of the various regions, and if it had appeared to them, they would have transmitted it as a mass-transmitted report (mutawatir), because human nature is disposed to spreading wonders. But it is possible that Allah concealed it from them by a cloud.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 2:**

﴿And if they see a sign,﴾ meaning the people of Makkah,

﴿a sign﴾ that indicates the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they turn away﴾ from believing in him,

﴿and say, "It is continuous magic."﴾ That is, firm and strong, from *al-marrah* (ʾal-marrah), meaning *al-quwwah* (strength); or constant and continuous; or passing and going away, vanishing and not remaining.

﴿And they denied﴾, the Prophet ﷺ,

﴿and followed their desires﴾, and what Satan had made attractive to them of repelling the truth after it had become manifest,

﴿and every matter﴾, what Allah had promised them,

﴿is settled﴾, existing at its appointed time. It is also said: every decree is certain to occur. It is also said: every matter of theirs is certain and settled, meaning: it will be confirmed and settled when punishment and reward become manifest.

﴿Wisdom﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, a noun in apposition that replaces the preceding word) for "ما" (mā), or it is in apposition to "هُوَ حِكْمَةٌ" (huwa ḥikmatun), "it is wisdom."

﴿Far-reaching﴾ means the utmost of correctness. Or "بالِغَةٌ" (bāligha) is taken to mean reaching from God to them.

﴿But warnings avail nothing﴾: "ما" (mā) is a negation particle. "اَلنُّذُرُ" (al-nudhur) is the plural of "نَذِيرٌ" (nadhīr, warner), and the warners are the messengers. Or it means what is warned against. Or "اَلنُّذُرُ" (al-nudhur) is a verbal noun with the meaning of "اَلْإنْذارُ" (al-indhār, warning).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 6:

﴿So turn away from them﴾, since you know that warning will not benefit them. ﴿The Day the Caller calls﴾ is in the accusative case (naṣb), governed by "yakhrujūn" (they will come out), or by the implied "udhkur" (remember). "Al-Dā‘ī" (the Caller) is read as "al-dā‘i" and "ilā al-dā‘i" by Sahl, Ya‘qub and Makki in both places; Madani and Abu ‘Amr agree with them in continuous recitation (waṣl). Whoever drops the yā' (the final ya') is satisfied with the kasra (vowel of the i) in its place. The omission of the waw from "yad‘u" in the written text (kitaba) follows the pronunciation (lafẓ). "Al-Dā‘ī" (the Caller) is Isrāfīl, upon him be peace.

﴿To a thing dreadful﴾, a terrible, frightful matter, which souls find repugnant because they have never experienced its like, and it is the terror of the Day of Resurrection. "Nukr" with the lightened pronunciation (takhfīf) is read by Makki.

"Khāshi'an abṣāruhum" (with their eyes humbled). "ʿIrāqiyyun ghayra ʿāṣim" (a reading in which the words are read as they are). This is a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) relating to "al-khārijīn" (those who come forth). It is the verb of "al-abṣār" (the eyes), and it is made masculine, as you would say "yakhshaʿu abṣāruhum" (their eyes are humbled). Others read "khushshaʿan" (plural), taking it as "yakhshaʿna abṣāruhum" (their eyes are humbled), and this is the dialect of those who say "akalūnī al-barāghīthu" (the fleas ate me). It is also permissible for the pronoun in "khushshaʿan" to refer to them, with "abṣāruhum" standing in apposition to it. The humbling of the eyes is a metaphor for abasement, because the abasement of the humbled and the pride of the mighty show in their eyes.

﴿Yakhrujūna min al-ajdāth﴾ (they will come forth from the graves),
from (p. 401) the graves.

﴿Ka-annahum jarādun muntashir﴾ (as if they were scattered locusts), in their multitude and their dispersal in every direction. The locust is a figure for multitude and surging motion, and it is said of a large army surging with its parts among one another: "they came like locusts."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 8:

﴿Hastening towards the caller﴾, rushing, extending their necks towards him,

﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾, hard, severe.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 9:

﴿Before them the people of Noah denied⁠—﴾, before the people of Makkah,

﴿and they denied Our servant﴾, Noah (peace be upon him). The meaning of the repetition of denial is that they denied him with denial following upon denial: whenever a generation of them that denied passed away, it was followed by another generation that denied. Or [the meaning is]: "The people of Noah denied the messengers, so they denied Our servant," that is, since they were deniers of the messengers, rejecting prophethood outright, they denied Noah because he is one of the messengers.

﴿And they said, "He is mad,"﴾ that is, he is mad.

﴿And he was rebuked﴾: it is said that he was prevented from conveying the message by abuse, and was threatened with killing. Or, it is part of what they said, that is: they said, "He is mad, and the jinn have rebuked him, have struck him with madness, and have taken away his reason."

﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنِّي﴾ That is: that,

﴿مَغْلُوبٌ﴾, "[I am] overcome. My people have overpowered me, and they have not listened to me, and despair of their responding to me has become firm,"

﴿فانْتَصِرْ﴾, "so avenge me against them, with a punishment that You send down upon them."

﴿So We opened the gates of heaven﴾, "فَفَتَّحْنا" (fattahnā, with the doubled letter), is the reading of al-Shāmī, Yazīd, Sahl and Ya'qūb.

﴿with water pouring forth﴾: pouring down, abundant and continuous, not ceasing for forty days.

And We caused the earth to gush forth with springs, and made the whole earth as though it were springs gushing forth, and this is more eloquent than your saying: "And We caused the springs of the earth to gush forth,"

﴿So the waters met﴾, that is: the waters of the sky and the earth. It is also recited as "al-māˀān" (the two waters), meaning the two kinds of water: the heavenly and the earthly.

﴿for a matter already decreed﴾, upon a state which God ordained however He willed; or upon a matter that had already been decreed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to come to pass, namely the destruction of the people of Noah by the flood.

(p-402) ﴿And We carried him upon [a vessel] of planks and nails﴾. He meant the ship. The word "vessel" (safīna) is one of the attributes that stand in for the things they describe: it takes their place and performs their function, such that no separation is made between it and what it describes. Similar to this is the verse:

"...but my shirt is a coat of chain mail woven of iron"

He meant: "but my shirt is a coat of mail (dir')." Do you not see that if you combined the ship with this attribute, it would not be correct? This is one of the eloquent and wondrous features of speech. And "al-dusur" is the plural of "dissar," which is the nail (al-mismār), on the pattern of "fi'āl," from "dasarahu," meaning he pushed it, because it is driven in (yudsaru) with it through its opening.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 14:

﴿Sailing under Our eyes﴾, in Our sight, or under Our protection, or "under Our eyes" is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in "sailing" (tajrī), meaning: "preserved by Us,"

﴿as a reward﴾, is an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu) for what was mentioned before, namely the opening of the gates of heaven, and what follows it, meaning: We did that as a reward,

﴿for him who had been disbelieved﴾, he is Noah, peace be upon him, and He made him one who was disbelieved, because the Prophet is a blessing from God and a mercy. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We have not sent you, except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:107]. So Noah was a blessing that was disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 15:

﴿And We left it as a sign﴾: that is, the ship (al-safina), or the deed (al-fa'la), meaning: We made it ﴿a sign﴾ by which one may take heed. It is related from Qatada: "Allah preserved it upon the land of al-Jazira." It was also said: it remained upon al-Judi (Mount Judi) for a long age, until the earliest members of this community looked upon it.

﴿So is there any who will take heed?﴾ — one who admonishes himself, takes heed and draws a lesson. Its original form is "mudtakir" with the dhal and the ta'. But the ta' was replaced by a dhal, and the dhal and the dal share a point of articulation, so the dhal was assimilated into the dal (idgham).

﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ The word *nudhur* is the plural of *nadhir* (warner), and *al-indhar* means warning. The reading *wa-nudhuri* (with the *ya'* at the end) is attributed to Ya'qub in both places where it occurs. Sahl agreed with him in the connected reading (*wasl*), while the other readers wrote both forms without the *ya'*. This same difference applies to what follows until the end of the surah.

We have made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so easy for taking heed and being admonished, by filling it with healing admonitions, and by varying in it the promise and the warning.

﴿So is there anyone who will remember?﴾ That is, anyone who will be admonished and take heed. It was also said: "And We have made it easy for memorization, and We have helped whoever wishes to memorize it. So is there anyone seeking to memorize it, so that he may be helped in it?" It is related that the books of the People of the Scriptures, such as the Torah (al-Tawrat), the Gospel (al-Injil) and the Psalms (al-Zabur), are not recited by their people except that they look into them, and they do not memorize them outwardly as the Qur'an is memorized.

Translation:

﴿Ad denied, so how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ That is: My warnings to them of the punishment before its descent, or: My warnings in their punishment to those who came after them.

Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind (ṣarṣaran), (meaning) cold, or having a severe sound,

on a day of misfortune (naḥs), (meaning) ill omen,

persistent (mustamirr), (meaning) constantly bringing evil; it persisted against them until it destroyed them. It was on a Wednesday (Arbi'a), at the end of the month.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 20:

﴿Tanzi‘u al-nas﴾ (it uproots people), it tears them up from their places. They used to line up, each holding the hand of another, and they would enter into the ravines and dig pits, hiding themselves in them, but it (the wind) would pull them out, overturn them, and smash their necks.

﴿Ka’annahum a‘jazu nakhlin munqa‘ir﴾ (as if they were the trunks of palm trees uprooted): the roots of palm trees pulled up from their planting places. They were likened to the trunks of palm trees because the wind would sever their heads, leaving bodies without heads, so they would fall to the ground dead, while they were tall bodies, like the trunks of palm trees, which are their roots, without branches. He made the attribute "nakhl" (palm trees) masculine in agreement with the wording (lafz); had he taken it in agreement with the meaning (ma‘na), he would have made it feminine, as in His words: ﴿Ka’annahum a‘jazu nakhlin khawiyah﴾ (as if they were the trunks of hollow palm trees) [al-Haqqah: 7].

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 54, verse 24:**

﴿They said, "Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾ The word *basharan* (بَشَرًا) is in the accusative case (*naṣb*), governed by a verb implied by the verb that explains it, *nattabiʿuhu* (نَتَّبِعُهُ, "we follow him"). The sense is: "Shall we follow a human being from among us, a single one?!"

﴿Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.﴾ He used to say: "If you do not follow me, you will be in error, away from the truth." *Suʿur* (سُعُرٍ) means fires, the plural of *saʿīr* (سَعِيرٌ). They reversed the charge against him and said: "If we follow you, we will be just as you describe us." It is also said that *ḍalāl* (اَلضَّلالُ) means error, mistake, and deviation from what is correct, and *suʿur* (اَلسُّعُرُ) means madness.

Their words *"a human being"* (*basharan*) express a denial that they should follow someone of their own kind in nature, and they demanded that he be one of the angels. They said *"from among us"* because, if he were from among them, the likeness would be stronger. They said *"a single one"* as a denial that a whole community should follow one man. Or they meant *"a single one"* from among their clans, not the noblest or most excellent of them. The following statement of His indicates this:

[p. 404]

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 25:

﴿Has the Reminder been cast upon him from among us?﴾ That is: Has the revelation been sent down to him from among us, while among us there are those who are more deserving than him of being chosen for prophethood?! ﴿Nay, he is a liar, an insolent one﴾, wanton and arrogant. His wantonness and his desire to exalt himself over us have driven him to claim this.

Surah 54 (al-Qamar), verse 26:

﴿They will know tomorrow﴾ — when the punishment descends upon them, or on the Day of Resurrection —

﴿who is the liar, the insolent one?﴾ — is it Salih, or the one who denied him? "Sa-ta'lamun" (you will know), is the reading of al-Shami (Ibn 'Amir) and Hamza, according to the narration of what Salih said to them, answering them; or it is the speech of Allah, by way of iltifat (a shift in grammatical person).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them﴾: We are sending her forth (bāʿithūhā, "raising her up") and bringing her out (mukhrijūhā) from the rock (al-haḍbah), as they asked.

﴿as a trial for them﴾ (fitnatan lahum): a test for them (imtiḥānan lahum), and a probation (ibtilāʾan). It is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose, "for the sake of"), or a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, "as a trial").

﴿So watch them﴾ (fārtaqibhum): wait for them (fānẓur-hum), and observe what they will do (wa-tabaṣṣar mā hum ṣāniʿūn).

﴿And be patient﴾ (waṣṭabir): over their harm (ʿalā adhāhum), and do not hasten until My command comes to you (wa-lā taʿjal ḥattā yaʾtiyaka amrī).

﴿And inform them that the water is to be shared between them﴾, divided among them: for her there is a day's drinking, and for them there is a day's drinking. He said "between them" (bayna-hum), giving precedence to the rational beings (taghlib li-l-'uqala').

﴿Every drinking [turn] shall be attended﴾, i.e., mahdur: the people attend the drinking on one day, and the she-camel attends on another day.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 29:

﴿So they called to their companion﴾, Qidar ibn Salif, the little reddish one of Thamud,

﴿and he took it in hand﴾, meaning he dared to undertake the great matter (taʿāṭī al-amr al-ʿaẓīm), being unconcerned about it,

﴿and hamstrung it﴾, that is, the she-camel; or, he took up the she-camel and hamstrung her; or, he took up the sword (al-sayf) and hamstrung her. He said ﴿they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 77] in another verse, because they approved of it, or because he hamstrung her with their assistance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 31:

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them﴾, on the fourth day after they hamstrung her (the she-camel),

﴿a single cry﴾; Jibril (peace be upon him) cried out at them,

﴿so they became like the dry branches of the one who fashions an enclosure﴾. And "al-hashim" (الهشيم): dry, brittle, crumbled vegetation that has broken apart. And "al-muhtazir" (المحتظر): the one who builds a hazira (enclosure). What is enclosed with it dries out over the passage of time, and the beasts trample it so that it shatters and crumbles. Al-Hasan read (الظاء) with a fatha (المحتظَر), which is the place of enclosing, i.e., the hazira (enclosure).

﴿We sent upon them﴾, meaning upon the people of Lut,

﴿a violent wind﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40], a wind that pelts them with stones, that is, hurls them at them,

﴿except the family of Lut﴾: his two daughters, and those who believed with him,

﴿We rescued them at dawn﴾, one of the pre-dawn hours. That is why it is declined (ṣarafahu, from ṣarf, "declension," the addition of nunation to the noun). It is said: "I met him at saḥar," when you met him at the dawn of his day. It is also said there are two saḥars: the upper saḥar, before the splitting of the dawn (infiṣād al-fajr, the first emergence of light across the horizon), and the other, at the moment of its splitting.

Verse 35 of Surah al-Qamar (54) is quoted here. The passage is a short grammatical and exegetical note from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil.

**﴿Grace﴾**, is a direct object of purpose (maf'ul lahu, the object of purpose), meaning: as a bestowal (in'am),

﴿from Us. Thus do We reward those who give thanks﴾ for the grace of Allah by their faith and their obedience.

And indeed he had warned them (﴿وَلَقَدْ أنْذَرَهُمْ﴾): Lot, peace be upon him.

﴿بَطْشَتَنا﴾: our seizing (أخْذَتَنا) them with punishment.

﴿فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُذُرِ﴾: so they disputed about the warnings (فَكَذَّبُوا بِالنُذُرِ), doubting them (مُتَشاكِّينَ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 37:

﴿And they had certainly solicited him concerning his guests﴾: they sought from his guests the act of immorality.

﴿So We obliterated their eyes﴾: We made them blind. It was also said: We wiped them away and made them like the rest of the face, with no slit visible in them. It is narrated that when they tried to force the door of Lut, peace be upon him, to enter, the angels said: "Leave them to enter. We are the messengers of your Lord; they will not reach you." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, struck them with his wing in one blow, and left them groping about and unable to find the door, until Lut brought them out.

﴿So taste﴾: I said to them, "Taste," through the tongues of the angels.

﴿My punishment and warnings﴾

Surah 54, verse 38, in the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿And certainly a morning punishment settled upon them at dawn,﴾ — "bukrah" (early morning), the beginning of the day.

﴿a punishment that is established,﴾ — thābit, which has become firmly settled upon them, until it leads them on to the punishment of the Hereafter.

The benefit of repeating ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings﴾ [al-Qamar: 37] and ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 40] is that, whenever they hear any account of the accounts of the earlier peoples, they may renew their remembrance and admonition, and begin again their alertness and awakening when they hear the exhortation to that and the urging toward it. This is the ruling on the repetition in His words ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [ar-Rahman: 13], at every blessing He enumerates, and in His words ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat: 34], at every sign He presents. Likewise is the repetition of the reports and stories in themselves, so that those lessons may be present in the hearts, pictured in the minds, remembered, and not forgotten at any time.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 54, verse 41:

﴿And there had certainly come to the family of Pharaoh the warnings.﴾ [They were] Musa, Harun, and others of the prophets, or it is the plural of *nadhir* (warner), and it is the *indhar* (warning).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 42:

﴿They denied Our signs, all of them﴾, meaning the nine signs.

﴿So We seized them with the seizing of One Almighty﴾, who cannot be overcome.

﴿Omnipotent﴾, nothing can frustrate Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 43:

﴿Are your disbelievers﴾, O people of Makkah,

﴿better than those⁠—﴾ the disbelievers mentioned, the people of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut, and the family of Fir'awn? That is: are they superior in strength, equipment, and standing in the world, or less disbelieving and obstinate?! The meaning is: your disbelievers are like those, rather, worse than them,

﴿or do you have a release in the Zubur?﴾ Or has a release been sent down to you, O people of Makkah, in the earlier scriptures, that whoever among you disbelieves and denies the messengers would be safe from the punishment of Allah, so that you feel secure because of that release?!

﴿Am yaqūlūna naḥnu jamīʿun﴾: a group (jamāʿa), our affair is united.

﴿Muntaṣirun﴾: able to defend itself (mumtaniʿ), we cannot be attacked (lā nurāmu), nor can we be wronged (wa-lā nuḍāmu).

**Surah 54, verse 45, from al-Nasafi's Madarik al-Tanzil:**

﴿Soon will the multitude be put to flight﴾: the multitude (jam') of the people of Makkah.

﴿And they will turn their backs﴾: i.e., the backs (al-adbar), as the poet said:

*"Eat in some part of your bellies, so that you may refrain..."*

That is, they will turn away in defeat, meaning on the day of Badr. This is among the signs of prophethood (ʿalamat al-nubuwwah).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 46:

﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time﴾: their appointed time of punishment, after (the battle of) Badr.

﴿And the Hour is more calamitous (adhā) and more bitter﴾: more severe than the standing (of the day) of Badr. And "al-dāhiyah" (the calamity) is a matter that is abhorrent, for which no remedy can be found.

﴿And bitterer﴾ in taste, than the punishment of this world, or more severe, from "al-marrah" (bitterness).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 48:

﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire﴾, they are pulled into it,

﴿upon their faces﴾, and it will be said to them,

﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾, like your saying: "He found the touch of fever, and tasted the taste of the beating," because when the Fire reaches them with its heat, it is as if it touches them with that touch. "Saqar" is not diptote (ghayr munsarif) due to the feminine gender and definiteness, because it is a proper name (alam) for Jahannam, from "saqarathu al-nar" (the Fire scorched him), when it burns him (lawahathu).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 49:

﴿Indeed, We have created everything in measure.﴾ "Kulla" (every) is in the accusative, governed by a verb understood, which the apparent verb explains. It is also read in the nominative, but this reading is anomalous (shadhdh), and the accusative is preferable, because if it were in the nominative, it would be possible for "khalaqnahu" (We created it) to be in the genitive position as a qualifying phrase (sifah) for "shay'" (thing), with the predicate being "bi-qadar" (in measure). Its estimated sense would be: "Indeed, every thing created by Us is in measure." It is also possible that "khalaqnahu" is the predicate, its estimated sense being: "Indeed, every thing created by Us is in measure." When the matter became ambiguous regarding the nominative, the accusative was chosen, its estimated sense being: "Indeed, We have created every thing in measure." Thus creation is general to every thing, and this is the intended meaning of the verse. In the accusative reading it is not permissible for "khalaqnahu" to be a qualifying phrase for "shay'", because it is the explanation of the governing verb, and a qualifier does not govern the qualified noun. "Al-qadar" and "al-qadr" both mean "al-taqdir" (determination), i.e., with a prior determination, or "We created every thing determined, firmly arranged, in accordance with what wisdom required," or "determined, written in the Preserved Tablet, known before its existence; We knew its state and its time." Abu Hurayrah said: "The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet (ﷺ), disputing with him about qadar, and this verse was revealed." And ʿUmar used to swear that it was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 50:

﴿And Our command is but one [word], like a glance of the eye.﴾ (Qur'an 54:50)

That is: "one word," meaning: Our command concerning anything We wish to bring into existence is only that We say to it: "Be," and it is.

﴿Like a glance of the eye.﴾ That is, in the measure of the time it takes one of you to glance with his eye. It was also said: the intended meaning of "Our command" is the Final Hour, as in His saying: ﴿And the command of the Hour is but like a glance of the eye﴾ (Qur'an 16:77).

(p-408) ﴿And We have certainly destroyed your likes﴾, your counterparts in disbelief from among the nations.

﴿So is there any who will take heed?﴾, any who will be admonished.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 52:

﴿And everything they have done﴾: that is, those disbelievers. That is, every deed done by them is recorded [lit. "is established for them"],

﴿is in the scriptures﴾, in the registers of the recording angels (al-hafaza). As for "fa'aluhu" (فَعَلُوهُ), it is in the genitive position (fi mawdi' jarr) as a qualifying adjunct (na't) of "shay'" (شَيْءٍ, "thing"), and "fi al-zubur" (فِي الزُبُرِ) is the predicate (khabar) of "kull" (كُلُّ, "every").

﴿And every small and great [matter]﴾, of deeds, and of everything that exists,

﴿is inscribed﴾, that is, written down in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 54, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and rivers﴾. [He] suffices with the singular noun denoting the kind (ism al-jins), and it is said: it means expanse and brightness, and from it comes the word "al-nahar" (daytime).

In a seat of truth, in a pleasing place,

in the presence of a King (ʿinda malīkin), an nearness of rank and honor, not of distance and physical contact,

Omnipotent (muqtadir), capable. The benefit of the indefiniteness (tankīr) in it is that it be known that there is nothing except that it is under His dominion and His power.
